title: Fewest Bricks Cut by a Vertical Line
statement:
A wall is made of rows of bricks, all rows the same total width. wall[i] lists the widths of the bricks in row i, from left to right. Every brick is 1 unit tall.

You draw one vertical line from top to bottom. Where the line runs exactly along the seam between two bricks of a row, that row is not cut; otherwise it cuts through one brick of that row.

The line may not run along the far left or far right edge of the wall. Return the smallest number of bricks it can cut.

examples.why: Seams at width 3 appear in the first three rows. A line there cuts only the 4-wide brick of the last row.
There are no inner seams, and the outer edges are not allowed, so every row is cut.
Each inner seam (at 1 and at 2) is shared by only one row.

constraints: 1 ≤ wall[i][j], and each row's total width is the same and at most 2 000 000 000
hints: Instead of counting the bricks a line cuts, count the rows it passes through cleanly.
A row is not cut at position x exactly when x is one of that row's inner seams, which are the running sums of its widths, excluding the last.
Count how many rows have a seam at each position with a hash map. The answer is rows minus the biggest count (or rows, if there are no inner seams).

explain.intuition:
Flip the question: cutting the fewest bricks is the same as slipping through the most seams. Each row's inner seams sit at the running sums of its widths, leaving out the full width at the end. A line at position x avoids a row exactly when x is one of those running sums.

So tally every seam position across all rows in a hash map. The busiest position is the best place for the line, and the answer is rows − busiest. Widths can be huge, so you never iterate over positions, only over bricks.
steps: Create a map from seam position to count.
For each row, keep a running sum over every brick except the last, and add 1 to that sum's count after each brick.
Let best be the largest count, or 0 if the map is empty.
pitfalls: Including the last brick's running sum. That is the right edge, which is forbidden, and it would make every answer 0.
Looping over every unit of width. The width can be two billion; only seams matter.
Returning the max count itself instead of rows minus it.

solutions.title: Test every seam position
solutions.idea: Collect all candidate seam positions, then for each one walk every row to see if it is cut.

solutions.title: Count seams in a hash map
solutions.idea: Tally inner seam positions across rows. The most shared seam is where the line goes.

followups: Return the position of the best line too. What do you return when there is a tie?
Rows are streamed one at a time and you cannot keep them. Does the approach still work?
